back: Organising data into tables to remove redundancy and update, insertion and deletion anomalies.
Every cell holds one value, there are no repeating groups, and there is a primary key.
In 1NF and no partial dependency: every non-key attribute depends on the whole of the primary key.
In 2NF and no transitive dependency: no non-key attribute depends on another non-key attribute.
A → B means each value of A is linked to exactly one value of B.
A repeated fact is changed in some rows only, so the data is inconsistent.
Insertion: a fact cannot be stored without another. Deletion: deleting a row also loses a fact you wanted.

front: Key, whole key, nothing but the key
back: A way to remember 3NF: every non-key attribute depends on the key, the whole key and nothing but the key.
Cambridge: normalise to 3NF. ZIMSEC: normalise to 2NF.
